claim: The KOSPI (South Korea's stock index) went up almost [200]% in the 12 months before [~late June 2026] [00:00]
quote: gone up almost 200% in the last 12 months
evidence: KOSPI closed 3,021.84 on 20 Jun 2025 (Korea Times) and hit an all-time closing high of 8,788.38 / intraday 8,933.62 on 1-2 Jun 2026 (KED Global, TOPONE Markets): (8,788-3,022)/3,022 = 190.7%, (8,934-3,022)/3,022 = 195.6% — trough-to-peak trailing ~12 months. 'Almost 200%' holds.

claim: The US S&P 500 only made [24]% over the same ~12 months, for comparison [00:00]
quote: the US's S&P 500, which only made 24%
evidence: S&P 500 closed 6,000.36 on 6 Jun 2025 (dshort/Advisor Perspectives) and set a record close of 7,609.78 on 2 Jun 2026 (CNBC): (7,610-6,000)/6,000 = 26.8%. Close to the stated 24% — same order of magnitude, small gap from using a slightly different anchor date within the same week.

claim: Samsung Electronics stock was up over [500]% at its peak this year [2026] [00:00]
quote: Samsung, was up over 500%
evidence: Independent data puts Samsung's actual 2026 move far below this: YTD cumulative gain hit 189% at its June 2026 record high (TradingKey), and the trailing 1-year gain was ~186%. Real and huge, but roughly 2.5-3x smaller than the '500%' claimed for 'this year' — a multi-year (2022-23 trough to 2026 peak) window gets closer to that magnitude, but the video says 'this year,' not multi-year. Kernel of truth, wrong timeframe.

claim: SK Hynix stock was up over [1,000]% at its peak this year [2026], 'basically a 10x' [00:00]
quote: SK Hynix was up over 1,000%
evidence: SK Hynix's own reported numbers: +167% YTD as of late Jul 2026, +430% trailing 1-year — both real and enormous, but 2.3-6x short of the claimed 'over 1,000%' for 'this year.' Even the 52-week high-to-low span (245,000 -> 2,987,000 KRW) is +1,119%, but that window straddles two calendar years, not 'this year' as stated — same wrong-timeframe pattern as claim 3, and the 'basically a 10x' gloss inherits it.

claim: Samsung and SK Hynix together represent over [56]% of the whole KOSPI [00:00]
quote: represent over 56% of their whole stock market
evidence: Combined Samsung+SK Hynix weighting was reported at 50.44% in May 2026 (Seoul Economic Daily) and topping 50% again in June coverage (KED Global); later coverage of the crash puts the pair at 'more than 50%' to '60%' depending on the week. 56% sits inside that range — moves day to day with the share prices, so this is confirmed as a range rather than to the decimal.

claim: South Korea has about [51] million people, and [14] million of them — one in four — are retail investors [01:04][03:12]
quote: there's about 51 million people. 14 million of them, or one in four, are what's called retail investors
evidence: Per the Korea Securities Depository (cited by Al Jazeera), stock owners rose from ~6 million in 2019 to 'more than 14.5 million at the end of 2025 ... more than a quarter of the total population.' Matches '14 million, one in four' closely; South Korea's population is ~51-52 million, consistent with the stated 51 million.

claim: In just [21] days, the KOSPI dropped [25]% [01:04]
quote: in just 21 days, everything started to collapse. The KOSPI dropped 25%
evidence: Headline 'Korea's KOSPI Plunges 25% in 3 Weeks' (BigGo Finance) — 3 weeks = 21 days, matching the video's window exactly. Independently, KOSPI 'had fallen 25% from its June peak' by 16 Jul 2026, with the peak dated to late June — same figure, same window.

claim: [1.2] million accounts got hit with margin call thresholds [01:04]
quote: 1.2 million accounts, which works out to be one in every 30 people in the country, got hit with something called margin call thresholds
evidence: 1.2 million accounts triggering margin calls is reported identically across multiple outlets (Eastern Herald, BigGo Finance, and others in the same cluster), all citing the same mid-July 2026 exchange/regulator figures — consistent, precise match.

claim: The margin-call accounts work out to about one in every [30] people in the country [01:04]
quote: which works out to be one in every 30 people in the country
evidence: 1.2M / 30 ~ 40M. Reporting states this is 'one in every 30 adults' (BigGo Finance), not one in 30 of the total ~51-52M population; South Korea's adult population is roughly 43-44M, close enough to the arithmetic. The video says '30 people in the country' rather than '30 adults' — a minor imprecision, but the ratio checks out against the reported basis.

claim: Over [3] trillion won in investments were liquidated [in the 21-day collapse] [01:04]
quote: over 3 trillion won in investments were liquidated
evidence: Multiple outlets cite 2.3 trillion won in forced liquidations — and that figure covers two and a half months, not the 21-day window the video frames it in. 'Over 3 trillion' overstates the reported total by about 30% and compresses a longer period into a shorter one — kernel of truth (a large, real forced-selling wave), exaggerated figure.

claim: The president of South Korea held an emergency intervention for the stock market [02:10]
quote: the president of South Korea held an emergency intervention for their stock market
evidence: Headline: 'South Korea Stock Market Plunges Into Bear Market After "Mad Bull" Rally: 2.3 Trillion Won Positions Forcibly Liquidated, President Steps In for Emergency Intervention' (36Kr) — directly confirms.

claim: Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta spent [$376 billion] on AI infrastructure in 2025 [06:26]
quote: they have spent $376 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025
evidence: Raised guidance during 2025 put the four companies' combined capex at 'more than $380 billion' (CNBC), and a separate aggregate estimate for 2025 AI investment runs to ~$400 billion; retrospective coverage of 2026 capex (claim 12) references 'last year's record $410 billion.' $376B sits below all three — plausible as an earlier-year guidance figure, but likely undercounts the final actual.

claim: Microsoft, Google, Amazon and Meta are on track to spend [$725 billion] on AI capex in 2026 [06:26]
quote: they're on track to spend 725 billion
evidence: 'Google, Microsoft, Meta, and Amazon capex spending to hit $725 billion in 2026' is a direct headline match (Yahoo Finance/Tom's Hardware, citing the same analyst note), and a separate outlet independently pegs the range at $720-745B — converges tightly on the claimed figure.

claim: In late June [2026], US chip stocks sold off because investors were nervous ahead of Micron's earnings [07:30][08:32]
quote: In late June, chip stocks in the US started selling off... nervous ahead of earnings from a very important company for the AI story, which is Micron
evidence: Micron reported fiscal Q3 2026 results after the bell on 24 Jun 2026; the prior day's ~13% chip-sector selloff was attributed by JPMorgan to 'anxiety before Micron's earnings, which tend to act as a gauge for AI demand' (Forbes), alongside a South Korean regulator ETF warning as a second, concurrent trigger the video doesn't mention. The video's specific causal claim is independently corroborated; it's not the only cause in play.

claim: In one session, the KOSPI dropped about [4.6]% [09:37]
quote: in one session, the KOSPI dropped something like 4.6%
evidence: Bloomberg headline: 'Kospi Index Slides 4.6% With Samsung, SK Hynix Falling on Chip Concerns', dated 23 Jun 2026 — exact figure match.

claim: A week later, Samsung and SK Hynix both fell more than [9]% in one day [09:37]
quote: a week later, Samsung and SK Hynix both went down more than 9% in just one day
evidence: CNBC, 2 Jul 2026 (9 days after the 23 Jun 4.6% KOSPI drop — 'a week later'): 'Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix shares tumble over 9% as chip rout spreads from Wall Street' — exact match.

claim: 'Black Tuesday': the KOSPI went down more than [10]% in a day — one of the worst drops in its history [09:37]
quote: the KOSPI went down more than 10% in just a day... one of the worst drops in the whole history of the Korean stock market
evidence: South Korean financial media named a single-session KOSPI drop of roughly 10-10.8% 'Black Tuesday' in late July 2026 — described as its worst single-session drop on record / largest single-day points decline in history. Different outlets give 9.99% and 10.84% for the exact print; both clear the '>10%' bar the claim sets, within normal same-event reporting variance.

claim: As of June 2026, US margin debt hit roughly [4.5]% of GDP — the highest ever recorded, higher than the dot-com bubble, 2007, and the 2021 meme-stock bubble [13:52]
quote: US margin debt just hit roughly 4 and 1/2% of GDP... higher than the dot-com bubble, higher than 2007, higher than even the 2021 meme stock everything bubble
evidence: FINRA-sourced margin-debt-to-GDP data (GuruFocus) shows a record 4.36-4.63% through mid-2026, 'surpassing the previous peaks before the burst of the internet bubble in 2000 (~2.3%), the financial crisis of 2008 (~3.0%), and the 2021 market high.' Matches closely; a couple of outlier estimates (5.2%) run higher but the mainstream FINRA-based figure lands right around the stated 4.5%.

claim: Every time US margin debt went to an extreme (1968, 1972, 1987, 2000, 2007, 2018, 2021), a crash happened almost right after, every single time [13:52]
quote: every time US margin debt went to an extreme, a crash happened almost right after, every single time
evidence: The 1987, 2000 and 2007 margin-debt peaks were each followed by a major crash, but the pattern breaks on the 2018 case the video itself cites: margin debt peaked in May 2018, yet the S&P 500 didn't top until October 2018 (5 months later) and the market then kept rallying into 2019, with the real crash (COVID) arriving nearly two years after the debt peak — not 'almost right after.' One of the seven cited instances doesn't fit the 'every single time' framing — a real correlation, oversold as an unbroken rule.

claim: Under normal conditions, about [2]% of Korean margin accounts get forcibly liquidated; during this crash the rate went above [10]%, about five times normal [10:40]
quote: under normal conditions, about 2% of Korean margin accounts get force liquidated... that number went higher than 10%, which is about five times the normal rate
evidence: 'The forced liquidation rate has surged from an average of 2.1% over the past six months to above 10% ... roughly a fivefold increase' (BigGo Finance) — matches the 2%->10%->5x claim almost exactly.

claim: Over the next two days, more than [$600 billion] got erased from Asian markets, and Japan fell more than [4]% [11:42]
quote: more than 600 billion dollars got erased from Asian markets... Japan went down more than 4%
evidence: 'Trading on both the KOSPI and KOSDAQ was halted on two consecutive sessions, and those two days erased approximately 864.5 trillion won — about $608 billion — in market value' is a near-exact match for 'more than 600 billion dollars ... over the next two days.' The Japan-specific >4% figure wasn't independently pinned to this exact two-day window, but broader regional losses of several percent across the same period are corroborated; rated on the strength of the headline $ figure matching precisely.

claim: Jim Chanos: hyperscalers' incremental operating income per dollar invested fell from about [40]% (a year and a half ago) to about [20]% now, heading toward [10]% [17:06]
quote: gone from as a group 40% a year and a half ago to about 20% today... it's going to be moving toward 10%
evidence: Reporting on Chanos's public remarks: 'hyperscaler incremental return on invested capital plunges from 40% to 20% and slides toward 10% ... this capital frenzy could face a brutal reckoning between late 2026 and 2027' — near-verbatim match to the video's quoted figures and framing.

claim: OpenAI and Anthropic together make up [70] to [80]% of all AI compute demand [18:12]
quote: they make up 70 to 80% of all the AI compute demand
evidence: Independent analyst estimates (Ed Zitron, cited across several outlets) put OpenAI+Anthropic at '70% of AI GPU compute capacity' and '85% of all AI compute spend' — in the same 70-80%+ range as the claim. These are outside analyst estimates, not disclosed company data (neither lab publishes compute-share figures), so this is capped at plausible rather than confirmed.

claim: OpenAI and Anthropic still lose tens of billions of dollars a year [18:12]
quote: they still lose tens of billions of dollars a year
evidence: True for OpenAI — reported 2025 losses range from ~$20.9B to $38.5B depending on methodology, with a further ~$14B loss projected for 2026. Not true for Anthropic by the time this video published: Anthropic reported more than $11.5B in Q2 2026 revenue and turned adjusted operating income positive in 2026, the opposite of 'still lose tens of billions.' Accurate for one company in the pair, stale for the other.

claim: In 2026, IPOs came to market at over [12]% of GDP in post-IPO market cap — more than double the previous dot-com-era record of [5]% [18:12]
quote: IPOs have come to market at over 12% of GDP in post-IPO market cap... the previous record was the peak of the dot-com bubble at just 5%
evidence: Searched multiple angles: overall US market-cap-to-GDP is at a record 238% (+90pp above the 148% dot-com peak), and 2026 IPO proceeds are running at ~$114-160B — real, record-setting activity including a single $1.77T SpaceX listing. But no source states the specific metric cited here — total post-IPO market cap of the year's IPO class as a share of GDP — or its claimed 5% dot-com-era comparator. Directionally plausible given SpaceX's size alone, but the underlying study or index was never located.

claim: The ~$725 billion in annual hyperscaler AI capex is roughly equal to the combined revenue of Nvidia, Micron, and 'the whole AI trade' [16:01]
quote: spending 3/4 of a trillion dollars a year, which happens to be the revenue of Nvidia, of Micron, and of the whole AI trade
evidence: Nvidia's FY2026 revenue was $215.9B and Micron's trailing-twelve-month revenue was ~$90.3B — combined $306B, about 42% of the stated $725B capex figure. 'The whole AI trade' is doing most of the remaining work and isn't a defined, checkable quantity, so naming Nvidia and Micron specifically alongside it overstates how close those two companies alone come to matching the capex number.

claim: Jim Chanos expects a reckoning sometime in late 2026 or 2027 [21:22]
quote: sometime in late 2026 or 2027... people are going to start putting pencil to paper
evidence: Same reporting on Chanos's public comments states the 'capital frenzy could face a brutal reckoning between late 2026 and 2027' — matches the quoted timeframe.

claim: In the S&P 500 ETF (VOO), the top 10 companies represent [36]% of the index [00:00]
quote: the top 10 companies represent 36% of this index
evidence: Contemporary readings put top-10 concentration at 37-41% through 2025-2026 (39.3% in May 2026, a 2025 record of 40.7%) — all somewhat higher than the claimed 36%. Same story (record concentration), but the specific figure sits on the low side of the range found; capped at plausible rather than confirmed given the gap.

claim: 320,000 accounts were wiped out, some of them overnight [02:10]
quote: 320,000 accounts were just wiped out, some of them overnight
evidence: Headline: 'Korea's KOSPI Plunges 25% in 3 Weeks, Triggering Mass Liquidations: 320,000 Retail Accounts Wiped Out Overnight' — exact figure match. Note: at least one other outlet in the same news cluster reports 360,000 for a similar/overlapping tally, so the exact number varies slightly by outlet and date.

claim: An anonymous investor in a documentary had a leveraged-ETF portfolio worth over [$650,000], up [150]% [05:20]
quote: Her portfolio was worth over $650,000, and she was up 150%
evidence: The investor is deliberately anonymous ('wouldn't even show her face on camera') and no documentary is named, so there's no way for an outside reader to verify her specific figures — a search surfaced other, non-matching Korean leveraged-ETF investor profiles (e.g. a named ex-dentist) but nothing matching this case. Unverifiable by construction, not evidence either way.

claim: At the peak, Koreans invested about [10] trillion won into leveraged funds betting on just one company [05:20]
quote: Koreans invested about 10 trillion won into leveraged funds betting on just one company
evidence: A real ~10 trillion won figure exists in this ecosystem, but it's daily trading turnover across 16 single-stock leveraged/inverse ETFs tied to Samsung AND SK Hynix (two companies, not one), with two SK Hynix products accounting for 65% of it. Separately, cumulative net purchases into these products totalled ~14 trillion won since the May 2026 launch, again across both stocks. Real number, wrong metric and wrong scope.

claim: Micron is America's biggest chip maker [08:32]
quote: That is America's biggest chip maker
evidence: Micron is the largest US-based maker of memory chips specifically, but not America's biggest chip maker overall — Nvidia (market cap ~$5.09T vs Micron's ~$991B; FY2026 revenue $215.9B vs Micron's ~$90.3B) is a US semiconductor company several times Micron's size by any common measure. True only with an unstated 'memory chips' qualifier the video doesn't include.

claim: A 10% one-day drop in the US stock market would be the third worst day in American history, only behind 1987 and the Great Depression [09:37]
quote: a 10% one-day drop in the US stock market, that would be the third worst day in American history, only behind 1987 and the Great Depression
evidence: Black Monday 1987 (-22.6%) is the record. But the ranking skips March 2020: the Dow fell 9.99% on 12 Mar 2020 and 12.9% on 16 Mar 2020 — both at or above a flat 10% drop, and both more recent than any Great Depression-era print. A 10% one-day drop today would land closer to 5th-6th worst, not 3rd, once the COVID-crash days are counted — reads like a pre-2020 fact ported forward without updating.

claim: In 2000, Coca-Cola needed 10,000 routers from Cisco; by 2001 they needed only 2,000 [20:18]
quote: Coca-Cola needed 10,000 routers from Cisco. By 2001, they needed only 2,000
evidence: Cisco's dot-com-era order collapse and $2.2B inventory write-off are extremely well documented, but nothing in that record mentions Coca-Cola specifically, or the 10,000-to-2,000 router figures, despite searches that surface plenty of other Cisco/Coca-Cola commercial history. The surrounding topic is well covered and the search is clearly working, which is what makes a named specific returning nothing worth flagging — a signal, not proof of invention.

claim: Cisco's earnings collapse coincided with the NASDAQ falling [78]% [20:18]
quote: the NASDAQ went down 78%
evidence: NASDAQ Composite fell from its all-time peak of 5,048.62 (10 Mar 2000) to a trough of 1,139.90 (4 Oct 2002) — a 77.4% decline, rounding to 78%. Matches exactly.

claim: DeleteMe was named the number one data removal service by Wirecutter [08:32]
quote: They were just named the number one data removal service by Wirecutter
evidence: 'In 2025, Wirecutter called DeleteMe the best data removal service' — matches. [Disclosure: sponsored segment] this is a paid sponsorship read (disclosed by the speaker as such), so the claim is about a real third-party award even though the surrounding endorsement is tier-4 advertising.

claim: In April 1912, the vice president of the company that owned the Titanic said 'We have absolute confidence in the Titanic. We believe the boat is unsinkable,' after it had already hit the iceberg and was sinking [23:30]
quote: We have absolute confidence in the Titanic. We believe the boat is unsinkable.
evidence: P.A.S. Franklin, vice president of IMM (White Star Line's parent/owning company), issued a statement on 15 Apr 1912 — after the sinking was already known — that the company was 'perfectly satisfied that the ship is unsinkable.' The video's wording is a close paraphrase rather than an exact transcript, and 'vice president of the company that owned it' is accurate once IMM-as-parent is accounted for.
